Node1 demand is node0 CURRENT order plus node1 backlog; node2 demand is node1 CURRENT order plus node2 backlog.
Unfilled demand becomes backlog. Next shipments to lower nodes are min(the next node demand including backlog, that next node inventory+arrival BEFORE its update). Node2 receives its own order without supplier constraint. All shipments enter a 4-period pipeline. Orders 0..20.
Primary cost=sum of inventory+backlog at ALL 3 nodes, coefficients all1. Also avoid increasing downstream backlog. An upstream reduction can starve downstream after delay; downstream extra orders can create upstream backlog. Observe all nodes and pipelines together.

message.content: {"candidates":[{"explanation":"Pipeline-aware relaxation with downstream protection. When total pipeline is high relative to recent delivered demand, cut orders modestly, but only if local backlog is low; if backlog exists, do not cut. When pipeline is low and backlog is positive, raise orders to protect service. Corrections are small and coordinated across nodes.","rules":[{"when":"pipeline > 3 * recent and backlog < 2","delta":"-min(2, max(0, (pipeline - 3 * recent) / 4))"},{"when":"pipeline < recent and backlog > 0","delta":"min(2, max(0, (recent - pipeline) / 2))"},{"when":"pipeline > 2 * recent and backlog >= 2","delta":"-1"}]},{"explanation":"Backlog-sensitive smoothing. Increase orders when backlog is high and pipeline is low, but avoid over-ordering when pipeline already covers demand. Downstream service is protected by limiting cuts when backlog is present.","rules":[{"when":"backlog > 2 * recent and pipeline < recent","delta":"min(3, max(0, backlog / 2 - pipeline))"},{"when":"backlog > 0 and pipeline < 1.5 * recent","delta":"min(1, max(0, backlog / 3))"},{"when":"pipeline > 2.5 * recent and backlog == 0","delta":"-min(2, max(0, (pipeline - 2.5 * recent) / 3))"}]},{"explanation":"Growth-adaptive damping.
